name: @cloudsforge/studio
description: Asset generation. Brand kits, asset specs, leased generation jobs and provenance-complete assets, generated through a reported image-backend chain with a per-account spend cap enforced before the call.

scripts._test: --test-concurrency=1 is required, not a preference: the database tests truncate this service's tables between cases, and node:test runs FILES in parallel by default. A TRUNCATE takes an AccessExclusiveLock, so one file's reset deadlocks against another file's inserts (40P01). Cases within a file already run in order.

_localDependencies: Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:'. A 'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of
these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a publishConfig that points main/types at dist/.
Packing therefore installs a package whose exports resolve to a dist/ that has not been built,
while its 'main' in the working tree still says src/index.ts. 'link:' symlinks the checkout in
place, so the working-tree manifest is the one that is read.
There is no image library here — no sharp, no jimp, no canvas. This service reads the exact
pixel dimensions a backend returned out of the PNG header and records them; see src/sizing.ts
for why recording 'unsized' beats shipping a resampler nobody can build in CI.
There is no openai SDK either. Azure's Images API is one POST and two response shapes, and the
SDK's model union is exactly what stopped asset-forge from naming gpt-image-2 at all.
